topic: Texas market reality check: price cuts, inventory, concessions, and the 60 day window
hook: Four in ten Texas sellers did this last month

scores.worst_problem: The hook leans on the tired "did this" construction and, given the topic, most readers will correctly guess "cut their price" before swiping, so the gap is thinner than it looks.
scores.fix: Rewrite slide 1 to withhold something less guessable than the obvious price-cut answer — e.g. lead with the two-speed contradiction ("Same street, same month: one house sold in 9 days, one has cut twice") so the reader cannot predict the mechanism.

deck.topic: Texas market reality check: price cuts, inventory, concessions, and the 60 day window
deck.hook: Four in ten Texas sellers did this last month

points.title: Four In Ten
body: Roughly four out of ten active Texas listings cut their asking price last month.
That is not a crash. That is sellers finally letting go of 2022 numbers.

points.title: Two Speeds, One Market
body: Priced right, homes here still go in under two weeks with multiple offers.
Priced on hope, they sit for months and cut twice.

points.title: Inventory Came Back
body: Texas is carrying more homes for sale than it has in over a decade.
Buyers can walk away now, and sellers know it.
points.loop: Sellers are already paying for it.

points.title: What Sellers Pay Now
body: Closing costs, rate buydowns, repairs, even the first year of taxes.
A large share of Texas deals close with the seller covering something.
points.loop: Not everyone gets the same deal.

points.title: The 60 Day Window
body: A seller who said no at day 20 says yes at day 70.
Nothing about the house changed. The math in their head did.
points.loop: The difference is measured in thousands.

linkedinCaption:
Roughly four out of ten active Texas listings cut their asking price last month. That is not a crash. That is sellers adjusting to a market that stopped rewarding 2022 pricing.

Inventory is the highest it has been in over a decade. Buyers have options again, and sellers feel it.

The split is stark. Homes priced correctly still move in under two weeks with competing offers. Homes priced on hope sit for months and cut twice. Same street, different outcome.

Concessions are now normal. Closing costs, rate buydowns, repairs, sometimes the first year of taxes.

And time changes minds. The seller who declined at day 20 often accepts at day 70.

What are you seeing on days on market in your submarket right now?
